update_cadence: Quarterly on earnings; SPV and private credit deals land unpredictably and need manual capture.
measurement_warning: The three measures below are not three estimates of one number. They are three different questions. Measure A asks what the companies owe as debt on their own filed balance sheets. Measure B adds contractual lease and purchase commitments they have signed but not yet drawn. Measure C adds obligations sitting in vehicles the companies do not consolidate — SPVs, leasebacks, private credit facilities to counterparties. Moving from A to C is not adding precision, it is widening the definition. Anyone quoting a single AI debt number is implicitly choosing one, usually without saying so.

leverage_ratios.source: Samsung Securities analyst Kwon Beom-seok, via Nikkei

companies.name: Oracle
companies.note: Excluded from the stable grouping. Oracle's five-year CDS widened roughly 70bp during 2026 to around 215bp, the largest move among major tech names.

leverage_ratios.interpretation: On this measure alone there is no distress. Debt/EBITDA under 1.5x is conservative for any industrial company. The analyst's own conclusion was that at current issuance pace there are at least two years before credit ratings come under pressure. This is the measure that makes the AI buildout look comfortably financed, and it is the measure that excludes most of the actual financing.

items.label: Signed but not yet commenced lease obligations across hyperscalers
items.source: S&P Global Ratings, cited in Chicago Booth Review
items.note: Excluded from funded-debt totals entirely. These are contractual obligations to pay that have not started and do not appear as debt.

items.label: Five-hyperscaler capital expenditure, 2026
items.source: KB Securities; corroborated by Yahoo Finance earnings roundup
items.note: Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta, Oracle. Up 4.9x from $148.1B in 2023. J.P. Morgan's comparable figure is $697B for the five largest, revised up $173B during the year. Company guidance: Microsoft ~$190B, Alphabet $180–190B, Meta $125–145B. Roughly $25B of Microsoft's and part of Meta's increase is component price inflation rather than more capacity.

measure_c_off_balance_sheet.label: Plus SPVs, leasebacks and private credit

items.label: Off-balance-sheet obligations, five companies
items.note: Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Oracle. Against roughly $1.35T in disclosed balance-sheet liabilities the prior quarter. Meta alone accounts for about $420B. Reported as an eightfold rise over four years. These are contractual commitments of varied kinds, not conventional debt with an immediate repayment obligation.

items.label: Off-balance-sheet obligations, nine companies
items.source: Wall Street Journal analysis, via 24/7 Wall St.
items.note: Adds Nvidia, Broadcom, AMD and SpaceX to the Nikkei five. Based on filings mostly current through June 2026. The jump from $1.65T to $3T is largely scope, not revision — do not read it as the Nikkei number being doubled.

items.label: Private credit loans outstanding to AI-related companies
items.note: From near zero a few years earlier. Principal lenders: Blackstone, Blue Owl, Apollo, PIMCO, BlackRock.

items.label: Data centre capex through 2028 not covered by operating cash flow
items.source: Morgan Stanley, via Lynk Capital Markets
items.note: Against ~$2.9T total global data centre investment through 2028, of which big tech operating cash flow covers ~$1.4T. Morgan Stanley's bridge for the gap: ~$800B private credit, ~$200B corporate bonds, ~$150B securitised products. This is the single most important number on the page — it is the amount of AI infrastructure that credit markets, not earnings, are being asked to fund.

items.label: US bank exposure to AI-adjacent industries, share of total assets
items.note: Chicago Fed cautioned that banks likely have additional indirect exposure through lending to the private credit funds doing the direct lending. The direct number is reassuring; the indirect channel is the one nobody has sized.

notable_structures.name: Meta Hyperion
notable_structures.structure: Blue Owl holds majority ownership of the vehicle; Meta is the tenant. Largest private credit data centre deal at the time.

notable_structures.name: Oracle / OpenAI Abilene, Texas
notable_structures.structure: SPV owns the facility, Oracle leases back. Roughly $10B of the $13B is debt.

notable_structures.name: Oracle Texas and Wisconsin package
notable_structures.structure: Debt package funding two data centres.

notable_structures.name: Anthropic compute SPV
notable_structures.structure: SPV buys the chips and leases them back. Debt is serviced from lease payments and stays off Anthropic's books. Apollo's financing arm owns the vehicle. If payments stop the chips are sold; Broadcom, the manufacturer, has agreed to cover any shortfall between sale proceeds and debt outstanding.
notable_structures.note: The manufacturer backstop is the structurally novel part. It links chip vendor solvency to data centre credit performance.

notable_structures.name: CoreWeave GPU-collateralised facility
notable_structures.structure: GPUs and customer contracts pledged as security. Split into investment-grade and speculative tranches. Variable rate averaged roughly 11%. Repayments began January 2026.
notable_structures.note: Repayment start coincided with a sharp decline in the market value of the collateral. This is the clearest live test of whether GPU-backed lending holds up through a price cycle.

securitisation.note: A roughly $25B ABS market facing take-out needs approaching $300B. Annual data centre securitisation ran near $27B in 2025; JPMorgan projects $30–40B in 2026 and 2027. The gap between market capacity and refinancing need is the plumbing risk.

ai_native_companies.label: Revenue and losses at AI-native firms
ai_native_companies.reconciliation_note: Revenue figures for private AI companies come from leaks, funding announcements and third-party estimates. They disagree. Where sources conflict the range is shown rather than a single value. Annualised run rate is not revenue; it is the most recent month multiplied by twelve, and it flatters fast-growing companies.

companies.name: OpenAI

booked_revenue_2025.note: Leaked audited statements verified by the Financial Times. Up from $3.7B in 2024.

annualised_run_rate.note: Roughly $3.3B/month. Held near $25B from February to May before an enterprise-driven breakout. Business revenue exceeded consumer for the first time in July.

operating_loss_2025.note: Leaked audited figure, against $13.07B booked revenue.

projected_loss_2028.note: Internal documents reported by the WSJ. Computing spend that year projected at $121B.

valuation.note: Flat at a $7B employee tender. Confidential S-1 filed June 2026.

cloud_commitments.note: $250B Microsoft Azure, $38B AWS over seven years, ~$300B Oracle over roughly five years beginning 2027. These are OpenAI's obligations and simultaneously the counterparties' backlog.

companies.unit_economics_note: Microsoft revenue-share data implies roughly $2 of cost per $1 of inference revenue before R&D, sales or overhead. Gross margin after inference around 48%, roughly half mature SaaS. Around 910M weekly ChatGPT users, of whom roughly 5% pay. Advertising began in the free tier in February 2026 and reached $1B annualised by August.

companies.name: Anthropic

annualised_run_rate.note: $47B confirmed in the May 2026 Series H announcement; a separate July figure of $65B is reported by Value Add VC. Trajectory: $87M January 2024, $1B December 2024, $30B April 2026.

quarterly_revenue.note: Up more than 50% sequentially. First recorded operating profit, described as small.

valuation.note: $65B Series H. Confidential S-1 filed 1 June 2026, targeting an October 2026 Nasdaq listing.

revenue_mix.note: Reported between 80% and 85% depending on source. Claude Code alone at roughly $2.5B annualised.

companies.burn_note: Burn projected to fall to roughly 33% of revenue in 2026 and 9% by 2027, against OpenAI's 57% holding steady through 2027.
companies.disclosure: This page was assembled with Claude, made by Anthropic. Treat the Anthropic figures with the same scepticism as the rest — they come from the same third-party sources, but you should know the provenance.

loss_per_revenue_dollar.note: Roughly $26 lost per $1 earned — the widest gap among major AI companies. Targeting profitability in 2027.
